 Toronto has opened the 2026-27 NBA season with consecutive victories, defeating the Chicago Bulls 135-92 before earning a 112-102 road win over the Washington Wizards. Scottie Barnes and Brandon Ingram have helped lead a balanced Raptors offense, while Immanuel Quickley provides another scoring threat in the backcourt. Toronto has also impressed defensively, allowing just 97 points per game through its first two contests, and will look to carry that momentum into a difficult matchup against Minnesota.
 The Timberwolves have been equally impressive, opening the season 2-0 with convincing road victories over the Miami Heat and Orlando Magic. Minnesota has averaged 123 points per game while holding opponents to just 99.5, establishing itself as one of the league’s most complete teams early in the season. LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards give the Timberwolves an explosive backcourt capable of taking over games, while Rudy Gobert anchors the defense. With both teams looking to remain unbeaten, Sunday’s matchup could provide an early measuring stick for two potential playoff contenders.
